chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Let no one intercede regarding a Hadd (fixed penalty) when it reaches the Imam, for he has authority over it. And intercede in what has not reached the Imam when you see remorse. And intercede before the Imam in matters other than the Hadd, with the return of the one for whom you interceded. And do not intercede regarding the right of a Muslim man, nor of others, except with his permission.'
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for valid intercession in Shia jurisprudence according to the Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the jurisprudential boundaries of intercession (shafa'ah) by distinguishing between divine fixed penalties (Hudud), where the Imam's authority is absolute and intercession is barred, and discretionary matters or individual rights, where it is permissible. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the Imam's judicial autonomy in Hudud while allowing for mercy in other contexts, provided the beneficiary consents, reflecting the balance between justice and compassion in Islamic governance.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘There is no interceding for anyone regarding a Penalty (Hadd) when it (the matter) reaches the Imamasws, for heasws controls it, and intercession is in what does not reach the Imamasws, when the (accused) shows the remorse, and the intercession in the presence of the Imamasws can be in other (matters) than the Penalty (Hadd), with the reference of the interceded to him, and one cannot inerceded regarding a right of a Muslim person, nor others, except by hisasws permission’.
